comparison.approach: Deliberately reads as an extension of hPanel rather than as a member of the AI-builder category: control-panel chrome, hamburger sidebar, credits meter with usage graph, purple Publish button top-right. Chat sits on the RIGHT (mirror of Remixer). One genuine craft detail: the chat panel drag handle resizes with persisted width, drag-to-hide, and double-click-to-reset. Plays a completion sound on publish.
comparison.notes: The visual bet is continuity with the hosting account, not membership of the AI category — a legitimate strategy and the closest structural analogue to Remixer, but it forfeits the premium read entirely. Undo/Restore are destructive with warning copy rather than designed checkpoints.

comparison.approach: Hybrid vibe-coding plus drag-and-drop editor with the Aria agent embedded in the visual editor. Landing hero is an open prompt field with a 'Refine my prompt' pre-flight button and four quick-start tags; persistent disclaimer 'AI can make mistakes. Always double-check the results.'
comparison.notes: No published design-language evidence, and its most distinctive motion moment is an anti-pattern — a 'Don't leave this tab' modal that blocks multitasking for the whole 4–7 minute generation. Generated output shows semantic failures (a sustainable clothing brief producing 'The Art of Food') and unlinked CTAs shipped live.

comparison.approach: Dark-only shell at a single stated #18181B, Inter/Gilroy/Proxima Nova, blue #1587FF for action, indigo/purple gradient as the AI brand mark, green = live, amber = action needed. Top toolbar with centred domain switcher and credits chip, ~408px left chat, right icon rail, centre canvas. Fastest first render in the field at 2–3 minutes, and the longest no-card trial (30 days).
comparison.notes: Three of the four documented AI-slop tells are in our own spec: Inter, an indigo→purple gradient, and a near-black that is cool-leaning (R24 G24 B27). Our accent sits three points from Bolt's #1488FC. No published elevation ladder, shadow ramp, radius scale or easing set — one shell hex is not a system. We are genuinely ahead on generation speed, trial length and structural position; we are behind on everything this lens measures.

best_in_class.why: It is the only product where the premium feeling is reducible to a system rather than to individual screens, and every layer of that system is independently verifiable. Colour: OKLCH semantic tokens where light and dark redefine ONLY the neutral ramp and the six semantic hues stay byte-identical (alpha .16→.2) — one brand in two themes with zero per-theme hand-tuning. Type: a proprietary variable face, Camera Plain Variable 100–900, self-hosted and licensed to Lovable Labs, used with intermediate axis values (prices at weight 480) that a static family physically cannot produce, and exactly two rhythms — display at line-height 1.100 / tracking -0.0400em at every size, prose at 16/24. Elevation: six dark surfaces ~2.5% lightness apart and a six-step shadow ramp whose offsets double geometrically (1/3/6/12/24px) with every layer at 4% black, plus a per-semantic inset bevel (`inset 0 1px 0 0 #fff, inset 0 -1px 0 0 #fffc`) that is the actual reason controls look injection-moulded rather than flat. Motion: four curves, 100–500ms, nothing bounces or overshoots, every reveal is the same single gesture (opacity + translateY 12px, IntersectionObserver-gated, not 40px, not a scale, not a blur), and hover/pressed exist as --glow-* tokens at 8%/16% alpha per semantic so every interactive surface in the product responds with identical weight. Waiting: ~39 named keyframes rather than a borrowed spinner — heartbeat (1→1.07→1.02→1.02→1.06→1, a literal double-beat on the logo), loader-sweep, shimmer-gradient, status-dot-ping (scale 1→2.667, opacity 1→0), and checkmarks DRAWN via stroke-dashoffset rather than faded in. Even the marketing hero shows discipline the rest of the field lacks: a live 2400×2420 canvas mesh gradient placed BELOW the fold line so 'Build something Lovable' sits on near-white and the gradient never competes with type for contrast. Nothing in the interface is Inter, and nothing is left to a browser default.

adopt.pattern: Replace the single #18181B shell colour with a published six-step warm dark elevation ladder
adopt.spec: Define six OKLCH surface tokens roughly 2.5% lightness apart, mirroring Lovable's dark ramp (20.42 / 23 / 24.74 / 27.2 / 30 / 32.8%) but rotated warm — hue in the 60–80 range at chroma ≤0.004 — instead of our current cool-leaning near-black (#18181B is R24 G24 B27, blue-leaning by 3 points). Assign roles explicitly: --surface-depth = app ground behind panels; --surface-base = canvas gutter; --surface-primary = left chat panel and right icon rail; --surface-secondary = message bubbles, cards, the credits chip; --surface-tertiary = hovered rows, inputs, the domain switcher; --surface-quaternary = popovers, menus, the publish dialog. Ban raw hex in components; every background must resolve to one of the six. Keep the same six roles when a light theme lands so only the values change.
adopt.rationale: Every serious competitor publishes a ladder, not a colour: Lovable six steps in dark, Bolt four (#111114/#171719/#1E1E21/#2C2C30), Base44 a full stone ramp. Base44's finding is that WARM surfaces are the cheapest 'expensive' signal available — cold Tailwind slate/zinc is the documented signature of AI-generated software, and Base44 never uses a pure cold grey for a surface. A single shell hex means panel-over-panel depth is being invented ad hoc in components today.

adopt.pattern: Get Inter out of the builder chrome; keep it available to generated sites
adopt.spec: Inter is named in the AI-slop literature as the tell ('Inter is a genuinely excellent typeface, which is exactly why it became the default and exactly why it now reads as generic'). Four of five majors run a proprietary or semi-proprietary face — Lovable's Camera Plain Variable, Vercel's Geist, Base44's Wix Madefor + Dazzed, GoDaddy's GD Sherpa + GD Sage — and the one that doesn't (Bolt) reads cheapest. Target state: one licensed or commissioned variable family for chrome with a display cut for headings. Zero-licence interim that captures most of the value: use a display optical cut for headings only, lock display line-height to 1.0–1.1 and tracking to exactly -0.04em at EVERY size (Lovable measures 48/52.8/-1.92, 36/39.6/-1.44, 28/30.8/-1.12; Bolt's h1 is 48/48/-1.2px), and hold body at 16/24 (1.5) with secondary body 14/24. Two rhythms total — 1.1 display, 1.5 prose — and no drift between them. Where a variable face is available, use non-integer weights (e.g. 480 for the credits balance and price strings) rather than snapping to 500.
adopt.rationale: Type is the single largest contributor to the 'expensive' read and the one competitors cannot copy in a sprint. The tracking-and-leading discipline alone is free and delivers a visible step change before any licensing decision is made.

adopt.pattern: Make 'metered' a first-class semantic intent, the way Base44 made 'premium' one
adopt.spec: Define a full intent alongside accent/positive/attention/destructive: --intent-metered-fill-{primary,secondary,light,ghost} × {default,hover,active,disabled}, --intent-metered-border-*, --focus-ring-metered (0 0 0 3px at 12% alpha), and exactly one --gradient-metered. Base the hue on our existing amber (action-needed) rather than inventing a gold. Bind it to every commercial surface: the credits chip in the top toolbar, the top-up button, the trial-days-remaining badge, per-message credit cost on hover of Send, the low-credit nudge above the chat input, and any publish gate. Hard rule for the design system: no control anywhere in Remixer may receive a bespoke 'upgrade' or 'limit' treatment outside this intent.
adopt.rationale: Base44 defines --sem-fill-premium-* with full state coverage plus its own focus ring and gradient, so every paywall reads as an intentional part of the interface instead of a nag. We are a credit-metered product with at least six commercial surfaces (credits chip, top-ups at +1,000/+2,500, trial expiry, publish gating, chat-edit cost, generation cost). Without one intent these will accumulate as unrelated one-offs, which is exactly how a product starts to look cheap.

adopt.pattern: Ship a six-step shadow ramp plus a two-layer inset button bevel; ban single-value shadows
adopt.spec: Surfaces: --shadow-xxs through --shadow-xl composed as a hairline ring plus geometrically doubling offsets — 1px/1px, 3px/3px −1.5px, 6px/6px −3px, 12px/12px −6px, 24px/24px −12px — with EVERY layer at 4% black, not the AI-default 10%. Tint the black warm (#1C1A18 per Base44) rather than pure #000. Buttons get a separate recipe simulating a lit bevel: inset 0 1px 0 0 rgba(255,255,255,.10) top highlight + inset 0 -1px 0 0 rgba(0,0,0,.30) bottom shade, with the top-highlight alpha raised to .16 on the blue Publish button so it reads as the primary. Add one specular trick for glass surfaces: --shadow-glass-top: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.08). Forbid any `shadow-lg`-equivalent single-value shadow in the codebase.
adopt.rationale: 'Subtle shadows (exactly 0.1 opacity)' is a named slop tell. Lovable's layered micro-lighting is explicitly the reason its controls look injection-moulded rather than flat, and Base44 achieves the same with 5%-alpha warm-black plus one inset highlight. This is the highest ratio of perceived quality to engineering effort in the whole dossier.

adopt.pattern: Adopt a three-duration, two-curve motion system with hover and pressed as alpha tokens
adopt.spec: Durations: --dur-fast 120ms (colour, opacity, focus ring), --dur-base 200ms (transform, panel and menu open, device switch), --dur-slow 300ms (overlays, modals, canvas transitions). Curves: --ease-out cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1) for entrances and state changes; --ease-standard cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1) for reversible chrome. No springs, no overshoot anywhere in the shell. Always enumerate the transitioned properties (color, background-color, border-color, box-shadow, transform, opacity) — never `transition: all`. Encode interaction weight as tokens rather than ad-hoc CSS: --glow-{accent,ai,positive,attention,destructive,neutral}-hover at 8% alpha and -pressed at 16% (neutral uses white at 4%/8% on our dark ground). Scroll reveal on marketing is ONE gesture only: opacity 0→1 plus translateY(12px), IntersectionObserver-gated, never scroll-linked, never a scale or blur. Honour prefers-reduced-motion by dropping transform and keeping opacity.
adopt.rationale: Geist's published guidance (~150ms state change, 200ms popover, 300ms overlay, cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1)) and Lovable's measured values (150ms opacity, 200–300ms transform on cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1)) converge on the same numbers, and Bolt runs a single 0.15s curve for everything. Base44 proves the token layer matters more than the values: because hover and pressed are tokens, every interactive surface responds with identical weight, and that consistency is a large part of the 'expensive' feel.

adopt.pattern: Rebuild generation choreography: name the design decisions, count the seconds, pre-dim the queue
adopt.spec: Three parts. (a) Left chat renders past-tense step rows at 13px in secondary text with a 16px leading glyph — 'Chose a warm editorial direction', 'Set colour theme and type scale', 'Built the hero', 'Assembled the page' — while the next three queued steps appear simultaneously at 45% opacity with a 1.6s shimmer sweep, so the user always sees a short-horizon forecast. (b) At least two rows must name a design decision in plain language, GoDaddy-style: 'Applied a warm espresso palette — paired with a serif display and a grotesk body.' (c) On completion the message footer reads 'Built in 2m 14s' beside a pulse glyph. Replace any indeterminate spinner on the canvas with a branded five-stop sweep bar in our blue: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent 0%, #1587FF 21.5%, #FFFFFF 33%, #1587FF 65.5%, transparent 100%) at 1.4s linear infinite, paired with rgba(255,255,255,.06) skeleton shimmer.
adopt.rationale: Bolt dresses a five-minute wait as precision machinery with a five-stop specular gradient token; v0 badges its own 6m21s as 'Worked for 6m 21s' and turns it into evidence of thoroughness; GoDaddy's sibling builder shows 'Worked for 45s' with a checklist that names the colour theme and font pairing. Naming decisions also gives non-designers vocabulary for the next instruction — 'warmer than espresso' instead of 'I don't like it'. We generate in 2–3 minutes, the fastest in the field, so an elapsed counter is a competitive statement, not an apology.

adopt.pattern: Reserve the AI purple to five surfaces and ban the gradient wash outright
adopt.spec: Indigo/purple is permitted on exactly five things: the AI sparkle glyph, the chat composer send button, the AI-mode chip, the generating sweep, and the landing-page composer halo. Everywhere else the interface is neutral plus #1587FF for action, green for live, amber for action-needed. Explicitly forbidden: purple gradients as section or hero backgrounds, purple card borders, purple headings, purple on any non-AI CTA. Separately, move our purple at least 12° of hue off the Tailwind indigo axis so it does not read as bg-indigo-500, and audit whether #1587FF should shift given Bolt sits at #1488FC — three points apart means our accent currently reads as category-default rather than proprietary.
adopt.rationale: GoDaddy's violet discipline is exemplary: it appears only on the BETA pill, alternating headline words, the prompt glow, the send button and the AI sparkle, and every non-AI control is neutral. Meanwhile 'an indigo-to-purple gradient' is the loudest named AI tell of 2026 — Tailwind's creator publicly apologised for making every button bg-indigo-500 'leading to every AI generated UI on earth also being indigo'. The purple-means-AI convention is worth keeping; the purple-as-decoration habit is what cheapens it.

adopt.pattern: Write three real empty states instead of blank panels
adopt.spec: (a) Canvas before first generation: logomark at 15% opacity plus one line of 15px secondary copy — 'Your site will appear here as Remixer builds it.' Nothing else. (b) Any panel loading project state: a centred 32px-tall pill, 999px radius, --surface-tertiary fill, 14px spinner plus 'Syncing project files…'. (c) Right-rail panel with nothing selected: teach three shortcuts as rendered keycap chips in a two-column list — Command palette ⌘K · Toggle chat ⌘B · Publish ⇧⌘P. Rule: never ship a bare panel, never ship the word 'Nothing here', and never ship a state that only apologises.
adopt.rationale: v0's three empty states each state what is happening or what to do next, and it uses the code editor's idle moment to teach four shortcuts with rendered keycaps (Go to File ⌘P, Find in Files ⇧⌘F, Command Palette ⇧⌘P, Terminal ^`). Base44's rule is that there is never an empty box, always a prefilled path plus an AI assist. Empty states are the cheapest craft signal in a product and the one most often skipped.

adopt.pattern: Commission a bespoke 16px icon family for chrome and keep the output's icon set separate
adopt.spec: Draw or commission a 16px family on a 16-unit grid at 1.5px stroke for the top toolbar, right icon rail, chat affordances and status glyphs. Keep Lucide (or whatever set generation emits) exclusively for generated sites. Bolt goes further and themes its terminal with the Hyper Snazzy palette (#ff5c57 / #5af78e / #f3f99d / #57c7ff / #ff6ac1 / #9aedfe on #171719) rather than shipping xterm defaults — do the same for any code or log surface we expose.
adopt.rationale: v0 draws its own 16-unit-viewBox icons for chrome while shipping lucide-react in output, so the chrome and the output are visibly different families. 'Thin-line, interchangeable icons' that 'could illustrate any product' are a named AI tell. If the builder's chrome wears the same icon set the builder emits, the product looks like one of its own templates.

adopt.pattern: Adopt a four-level finding icon language and reuse it for domain, SSL and publish states
adopt.spec: Four levels, one vocabulary, used everywhere: green check = passing; blue lightbulb = low impact / suggestion; amber warning triangle = medium impact / action needed; red X = high impact / blocking. Group results as Failing / Passing / Fixed / Ignored with a Restore action. Reuse the exact same four glyphs and grouping for domain status, SSL provisioning, publish readiness and any future scan, and pair each terminal red state with a recovery verb button (Check status / Retry / Recover / Reconnect) so no state is a dead end. Keep our existing semantics intact: green = live, amber = action needed.
adopt.rationale: Lovable uses one four-level icon language across security and SEO, and one three-word status vocabulary ('Up to date' / 'Out of date' / 'Scanning your project…') across unrelated subsystems — which is precisely why the product feels like one thing rather than a bundle of features. It also gives a recovery verb to every domain failure state, where GoDaddy ships a single 'Active' status and a 48-hour warning with no designed intermediate state.

avoid.pattern: Inter + indigo→purple gradient + three rounded cards in a row — the documented AI-slop fingerprint, which is currently our own spec
avoid.why: The 2026 critique literature names it precisely: 'AI slop design has a fingerprint: the Inter typeface, an indigo-to-purple gradient, three rounded cards in a row, and a hero section that could belong to any of ten thousand other products.' Tailwind's creator publicly apologised for 'making every button in Tailwind UI bg-indigo-500 five years ago, leading to every AI generated UI on earth also being indigo.' Remixer's stated design language is Inter/Gilroy/Proxima Nova with an indigo/purple gradient as the AI brand mark — three of the four tells, in the interface of a product whose whole promise is that it will not generate generic output.

avoid.pattern: Cold Tailwind slate/zinc as a surface colour
avoid.why: Base44 maintains two full neutral ramps and uses the warm one (stone #f8f6f4 → #1b1a19) for every surface, reserving cool neutral for disabled states and dark shimmer, and tints its shadows warm-black (#1c1a18 / #0f0e0e) rather than pure #000. Cold grey is the default of every scraped Tailwind tutorial and therefore the signature of AI-generated software. Our #18181B is blue-leaning by 3 points (R24 G24 B27) — technically neutral, perceptually on the cold side of the line.

avoid.pattern: Single-value shadows, and any shadow at 10% opacity
avoid.why: 'Subtle shadows (exactly 0.1 opacity)' is a named hallmark of generic AI design, alongside 'the untouched rounded-2xl shadow-lg p-6 shadcn default card'. Both premium systems in the field do the opposite: Lovable composes six steps with geometrically doubling offsets at 4% black plus a per-semantic inset bevel; Base44 runs 5%-alpha warm-black with an inset white top highlight. One shadow at one opacity is what a component library ships when nobody made a decision.

avoid.pattern: Changing visual identity between marketing and product
avoid.why: GoDaddy Airo's entry screen is the best single composition in this sweep — a white pill floating in a lavender bloom on near-black violet — and then the builder interior is light, with white chat cards and a light canvas. The product you fell for is not the product you use. Lovable does the opposite: the same ProseMirror composer, same tokens, same type is the marketing hero, the dashboard entry and the editor input, so muscle memory formed before signup transfers intact.

avoid.pattern: Decorative motion that is not a state change — pulsing dots, simulated typing, looping marquees
avoid.why: Vercel's brand guidance is explicit: 'Default to stillness. Never add auto-scrolling marquees, simulated typing cursors, or decorative pulsing status indicators,' and motion should 'explain a state change, preserve continuity, or confirm an action.' Note the live tension — Lovable's typewriter placeholder and status-dot-ping violate this and still read premium, because they are load-bearing (teaching prompt grammar, signalling liveness). The rule to enforce is not 'no motion'; it is that every animation must name the state it explains, or it gets cut.

avoid.pattern: An empty preview pane for the entire generation window
avoid.why: v0 shows only the logomark and 'Your v0 generation will show here.' for the full 6 minutes 21 seconds of a build, putting all the drama in the chat. That is a defensible bet at v0's technical audience, but for Remixer's audience it wastes the single best trust-building surface we have. Bolt at least dresses the wait with a five-stop specular sweep; Replit goes further and renders the agent's own cursor clicking through the app inside the pane.

avoid.pattern: A user-facing 'Refresh Preview' button, and dev-server language in a no-code product
avoid.why: GoDaddy ships '(Optional) If you don't see your edits updating, select Refresh Preview' and its official prompt guide lists the recommended fix for 'Preview isn't working' as prompting 'Restart dev server'. Shipping a manual refresh control is an admission that the preview desyncs, and leaking a dev-server concept into help text for a no-code audience breaks the abstraction the whole product is sold on.

avoid.pattern: Raw stack traces and framework errors surfacing to non-technical users
avoid.why: Base44's own troubleshooting page enumerates what users actually see: 'Failed to load app: Error serializing to JSON: UnicodeEncodeError' (triggered by unsupported characters in an app NAME), 'Uncaught Error: Error in json schema: properties is required for object type', and "'dict' object has no attribute 'lower'" — a Python AttributeError shown to someone sold a no-code product. GoDaddy hits the same class of failure with a bare 'Bad Request' on a long prompt, at the highest-intent moment in the funnel.

avoid.pattern: Blocking modals during generation
avoid.why: Wix Harmony shows a 'Don't leave this tab' modal mid-build, warning that leaving the browser tab would interrupt the generation, across a 4–7 minute wait. It converts a wait into enforced attention and tells the user the system is fragile. Every credible competitor lets you leave — Lovable queues further prompts above the input during the run; Replit lets you monitor progress from your phone.

avoid.pattern: Two names for the same control, and two surfaces for the same job
avoid.why: GoDaddy's docs call one device selector 'Preview Desktop' in the build article and 'Change device' in the publish article, and its top menu carries both 'Menu' (upload and insert images, videos, documents) and 'Media' (edit, upload and manage visuals) as separate asset surfaces. Naming drift is the visible symptom of a system with no owner, and it undoes the credibility that expensive-looking chrome buys.

avoid.pattern: Shipping copy with punctuation and grammar errors alongside premium visual craft
avoid.why: Bolt's marketing page contains real errors in shipped strings — 'Bolt gives you everything you need inside one familiar interface no extra accounts, no steep learning curve' and 'iterates reducing errors' — missing em-dashes in a page otherwise carrying a full token system, Inter Display optical cuts and a bespoke terminal theme. Copy craft and visual craft are read as one signal; one broken sentence discounts the whole surface.

avoid.pattern: Interface-wide gradient washes behind body copy
avoid.why: Lovable renders a live 2400×2420 canvas mesh gradient in the hero and still keeps 'Build something Lovable' on near-white (--bg-base oklch 96.99%), fading the gradient in only across the lower two-thirds so it never competes with type for contrast. The dossier flags this as 'a discipline most AI-builder landing pages break'. A gradient behind text is the fastest way to make an expensive page look like a template.

leapfrog.idea: Brand Seed — derive the site's design system from the domain, at the moment the domain is chosen
leapfrog.spec: In the domain step (search, or 'this domain is already in your DreamHost account'), render a Brand Seed card before generation begins. Inputs we uniquely hold at that instant: the TLD (.law, .cafe, .studio, .dev carry real category signal), the second-level name's phonetics and length, and — if the domain already resolves — the existing site's dominant palette, typefaces and image tone scraped at DNS-resolution time. Output: three named directions, each a 5-swatch palette, a display+text typeface pairing, a radius personality and a shadow weight, labelled in plain language ('Warm editorial', 'Clinical modern', 'Bold utility'). One click seeds the generation; the seed writes theme colours and font tokens BEFORE any component is built, which is exactly the ordering v0 uses ('Updated theme colors' → 'Added font tokens' → then header/hero/sections). Copy on the card: 'We read your domain. Here's where we'd start.' Store the chosen seed as the project's design system so later prompts are grounded rather than re-improvised.
leapfrog.why_nobody_does_it: Nobody else is standing at the registrar counter when the aesthetic decision gets made. Lovable, Bolt, v0 and Emergent all bolt a registrar on AFTER the build, so the domain is a distribution detail, not a creative input. GoDaddy owns the moment and squanders it: its Airo flow gives you 12 logo options and an LLC filing off a domain purchase, but the domain never seeds the site's design system, and buying a domain mid-build kicks you out to the storefront and back.
leapfrog.remixer_advantage: We are the registrar. We see the domain before generation, we can resolve it, and if it is already in the user's DreamHost account we know its age, its current host and its existing content — none of which any pure AI builder can obtain at prompt time.

leapfrog.idea: Your brand, in their inbox — compile the site's design tokens into a real mailbox and a previewed email theme
leapfrog.spec: When a plan includes a mailbox at the connected domain, compile the project's design tokens (palette, display and body typefaces, radius, button bevel) into an email theme and preview it in-builder inside a device frame beside the site preview — same tokens, two surfaces. Ship four templates by default: form-submission notification, order receipt, account welcome, and password reset. Then close the loop inside the 30-day trial: the first real form submission arrives at hello@theirdomain, styled in their own brand, in a mailbox they own. Copy on the panel: 'Your forms go to a real inbox you own — hello@yourdomain.com — and the email looks like your site.' Never send from a no-reply@ourdomain address.
leapfrog.why_nobody_does_it: Structurally they cannot. v0, Bolt and Figma have no email product at any tier. Lovable sends DKIM/SPF/DMARC-authenticated mail from your domain (50,000/mo) but states plainly it provides no mailboxes. Base44 is blunter still — 'Custom email domains are for sending only', default sender no-reply@base44-apps.com via SendGrid, and its built-in email cannot even reach an address that is not a registered app user, so a contact form emailing the owner's Gmail is not a first-class path. GoDaddy has mailboxes but resells Microsoft 365 at $7.99/mo as an upsell, and its contact-form configuration is done by pasting GoDaddy-authored prompts into chat rather than through any designed surface.
leapfrog.remixer_advantage: DreamHost operates its own mail platform. We can provision the inbox, own the deliverability, and design the message — three things no competitor can do together. This is the single durable gap now that Lovable, Vercel, Replit and even Emergent have all become registrars.

leapfrog.idea: One theme, every surface — extend the design system to the pages only a host controls
leapfrog.spec: Compile the project's tokens into every surface DreamHost serves that is not the site itself: the 503 maintenance page (we already have measured tokens and 503 rules from prior work), the coming-soon page shown while DNS propagates, the SSL-provisioning interstitial, the 404 and 500 pages, and billing receipts. Surface it in the right rail as a single 'Brand surfaces' panel listing each page with a live thumbnail and a status chip, so the user sees their own palette and typeface on a maintenance page they never designed. Copy: 'Even your error pages are on brand.' Default all of them on; let the user edit copy but not break the token binding.
leapfrog.why_nobody_does_it: These pages live at the hosting layer, below the application. Lovable, Bolt, v0 and Base44 deploy to an edge they rent (Cloudflare, Render, Vercel, AWS) and never own the failure surface — when their apps break, users see a generic vendor page or a white screen. Bolt's own free-tier sites simply go offline until the next billing cycle on bandwidth overage.
leapfrog.remixer_advantage: DreamHost runs the hosting and the CDN (SmartEdge, 10 PoPs), so we control what is served when the app is down, mid-deploy, or mid-propagation. Nobody else can make a branded 503.

leapfrog.idea: Propagation as a designed state machine, not a 48-hour shrug
leapfrog.spec: Replace the industry-standard 'it can take up to 48 hours' with a live, animated resolver view. Show the record we expect and the record each of our own resolvers currently sees, as a row per checkpoint with the four-level status glyphs (green check / blue lightbulb / amber triangle / red X), refreshing on a 15s poll with a 200ms crossfade — no spinner, no page reload. Name every state and give every terminal state a verb, as Lovable does: Verifying → 'Check status'; Records not found → 'Show me the records'; Conflicting AAAA record → 'Remove it for me' (which we can actually do for DreamHost-held domains); Stalled → 'Retry'; Live → the green chip in the toolbar. For a domain already in the user's DreamHost account, the whole panel collapses to a single line: 'Connected. No DNS changes needed.'
leapfrog.why_nobody_does_it: Everyone else is guessing from outside the DNS system. Bolt: 'Most domains connect within a few hours, but in some cases, it can take up to 24 hours' with a manual 'Verify domain status' button. Base44 sends users to whatsmydns.net — a third-party site — to debug their own product's DNS. GoDaddy shows a single 'Active' state and a 48-hour warning with no designed intermediate. Lovable is the best of them and still only has status labels, because it cannot see inside the user's registrar.
leapfrog.remixer_advantage: We are the authoritative nameserver for DreamHost-held domains, so propagation is not a black box we poll — it is our own data, and we can both display it and fix it in place. It also converts our known Domain Connect gap from an apology into a demonstration of the case where we are structurally better than everyone.

leapfrog.idea: Bind the design system to the DOMAIN rather than to the project or workspace
leapfrog.spec: Store the compiled design system (palette, type pairing, radius, shadow, motion set, logo, tone of voice) against the domain record, not the build. Consequences: rebuild the site from scratch and the brand survives; spin up a second project on a subdomain and it inherits; the maintenance page, email theme and coming-soon page all read from the same record; transfer the domain within DreamHost and the brand travels with it. Surface it as a 'Brand' entry in the centred domain switcher already in our top toolbar — the same control that switches domains switches brand context — with an 'Update available' prompt on connected projects when the record changes, following v0's rule that updating a system never silently rewrites existing work.
leapfrog.why_nobody_does_it: Nobody else has a durable object to attach it to. Lovable's design systems are versioned projects belonging to a workspace and gated to Enterprise; v0's design-system skills belong to a team; Bolt's Storybook-backed systems require a paid Team plan; Base44 allows one design system per workspace. All four bind brand to an account construct that dies when the account does. A domain outlives the project, the plan, and often the company.
leapfrog.remixer_advantage: We hold the registry record. Binding brand identity to the one asset the customer genuinely owns and renews annually creates a retention mechanic no application-layer competitor can construct, and it makes our centred domain switcher the most valuable control in the toolbar rather than a convenience.

open_questions: Do we own or can we license a UI typeface with actual personality? Four of five majors run proprietary faces (Camera Plain Variable, Geist, Wix Madefor + Dazzed, GD Sherpa + GD Sage) and the one on Inter reads cheapest. What are the cost and lead time for a commissioned variable cut versus licensing an existing non-Inter grotesk, and how widely deployed are Gilroy and Proxima Nova already?

Does Remixer's generated OUTPUT have a motion system at all, or only the builder chrome? Figma Make now accepts motion as an annotation ('fade this button in after a 300ms delay', 'add a subtle press effect when this button is tapped'), which implies generated sites are expected to ship hover, press and reveal behaviour. What do we currently emit, and is it tokenised or improvised per generation?

Is dark-only permanent? Bolt and v0 are dark-only and coherent; Lovable and Base44 both invest in real dual themes, and Lovable's dark is the design-led one with six elevation steps versus light's three. Our users' sites are overwhelmingly light — does previewing a light site inside a dark shell cost us design accuracy, and does the builder need a light theme for that reason alone?

Does publishing consume credits, and if so, how do we design that? Lovable states publishing is free and does not consume credits; Bolt bills tokens only for agent work; GoDaddy's published billable list excludes publish entirely. If our Publish button is metered, it needs a cost affordance, which is a design problem we created — is the revenue worth the visual and emotional tax on the moment of success?

What is our actual design system today beyond #18181B, #1587FF, green and amber? Is there a published elevation ladder, radius scale, shadow ramp, spacing grid and easing set, or are components inventing values? A token audit should precede any of the adopt items above.

Do we move #1587FF? Bolt's brand blue is #1488FC — three points away. Either we shift hue enough to be distinguishable in a side-by-side screenshot, or we decide the category-blue is worth owning and differentiate entirely on type, warmth and elevation. This needs a decision, not a drift.

Which manual edits should be free? Figma Make stages direct manipulation credit-free until you hit apply; Base44 exempts dragging, layout changes and direct text editing entirely; Replit's Element Editor writes source directly with no agent call; Lovable gives 100 free inline text edits per user per day. If nudging padding costs a credit in Remixer, our visual editor will be under-used and our token system will never get exercised.

Is the marketing site and the product one visual system or two? Lovable reuses the identical composer component across hero, dashboard and editor; GoDaddy breaks identity at the door (dark entry, light builder). Who owns the decision, and is the landing-page prompt box literally the same component as the builder chat input?

Is prefers-reduced-motion honoured in the builder AND in generated output? Vercel's guidance requires dropping non-essential motion; none of the competitor dossiers evidence it. This is both an accessibility obligation and, if we ship it in generated sites, a differentiator we can name.

Who arbitrates when the AI's chosen aesthetic conflicts with the Brand Seed or design system? v0's grounded generation 'refuses to use components, props, or tokens it cannot verify'; Lovable's Superblocks review found fine-grained design edits silently overwritten by later prompts because visual and chat edits write the same files with no protected-region concept. Do we need a lock or protected-token mechanism before we ship a design system at all?
